headline: Profiles, a repair for imported Plex history, and fewer disk writes
upgradeWarning: Back up before upgrading. tofa requests are stored differently from this release on, so going back to 3.2 needs that backup

highlights.title: Profiles
highlights.body: tofa and Silo accounts can have several profiles. Tracearr now records which profile played each stream and download, shows it as a small badge on the account avatar wherever plays appear, splits plays and watch time by profile on the user page, and lets History filter by profile. The main profile stays unlabeled. tofa plays from before updating pick up their profile after the first user sync.

highlights.title: Imported Plex history
highlights.body: After a Plex rebuild reused item keys, imported plays could show under another show or movie. Imports now take a library item by key only when the play and the item agree, and a repair runs once after updating to put existing plays back. Where many of a server's imported plays look mislinked, it holds back and asks: run Repair Imported Plex Links in Settings → Data → Jobs.

highlights.title: Silo
highlights.body: Tracearr monitors Silo servers: live sessions, library, history import, downloads, CPU and memory, and Silo's own requests. Add one with a code approved in Silo or an API key; members sign in with their Silo account. Silo is pre-release with no tagged releases and its API still changes, so a Silo update can break support until Tracearr catches up.

highlights.title: Fewer disk writes
highlights.body: Background jobs that walk history, such as identity matching, imported history linking, location sync and import cleanup, no longer decompress and rewrite old history they don't change. On a large history that means far less writing to disk.

changes.text: profiles on tofa and Silo: plays and downloads record the profile, Silo requests too, and History filters by profile
a play from a profile other than the account's main one shows that profile's picture on the account avatar
the user page splits plays and watch time by profile when the account has played on more than one
stream notifications, the public API, Downloads and media History also show a profile that isn't the account's main one
plays on tofa from before updating pick up their profile from tofa's watch history after the first user sync
Silo servers: live sessions, library, history import, downloads, CPU and memory, and Silo's own requests
add a Silo server with a code approved in Silo or with an API key; members sign in with their Silo account
History and the user page hide Quality and Progress when the table is too narrow; turning one on in Columns keeps it
background maintenance no longer decompresses and rewrites old history it doesn't change, cutting disk writes
history imports no longer skip the plays of an account merged into another on the same server as unknown user
after a Plex rebuild, imported plays no longer show under another show, and updating repairs the ones that did
the Plex link repair holds back where many imported plays look mislinked; run it in Settings → Data → Jobs
Silo support isn't an endorsement. Silo is pre-release with no tagged releases yet, and its API still changes
Silo changes land fast, often dozens of commits a day, so a Silo update can break support until Tracearr catches up
a Silo server's version shows as its build id, and Tracearr doesn't check it for updates
posters and uploaded avatars from a Silo server that keeps its artwork in S3 or R2 don't show in Tracearr yet
